clue.text: Belgian detective has a point — a strong one

parts.note: Hercule Poirot is Agatha Christie's Belgian sleuth, so his first name is taken
S, south, is a compass point

explanation.surface: Poirot is credited with having a sharp, forceful point to make.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a strong one' is the definition: Hercules was the mythical strongman.
explanation.definitionFit: Hercules, the Greek hero of the twelve labours, is the byword for a man of great physical strength.

clue.text: Always set out as height of ambition

parts.note: ever means always

indicators.note: out suggests the letters of set are put out of order, rearranged

explanation.surface: Being always set on a goal is the peak of aspiration.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges SET to EST, which follows EVER.
explanation.definitionFit: Climbing the world's tallest mountain is the summit every mountaineer aspires to, so the peak is the top of their goals.

parts.note: a man who takes care is meticulous, and the same title names Harold Pinter's play, so the man is named after it

explanation.surface: A fussy theatregoer follows every line of the drama.
explanation.walkthrough: Split as CARE TAKER it is one who takes care; it is also the title of Pinter's 1960 play, and the job of a building's janitor.
explanation.definitionFit: A janitor's job title split in two reads as one who takes pains, and also names a famous Pinter play.

clue.text: Book found in shelf on the right :

parts.note: a ledge is a narrow shelf

explanation.surface: A volume turns up on the right-hand shelf.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on the' just places R after LEDGE.
explanation.definitionFit: An account book in which a business records its transactions is a type of book.

clue.text: Glorified potting shed judging by reports

definitions.text: Glorified potting shed judging by reports

parts.words: Glorified potting shed judging by reports
parts.note: potting here is shooting at targets, and reports are the bangs of guns, so this is a shed for firing judged by its noise

explanation.surface: A gardener's shed sounds grander than it is, going by what people say.
explanation.walkthrough: 'potting' suggests plants in pots but means shooting, as in potting a rabbit; 'reports' suggests rumour but means gunshots.
explanation.definitionFit: A fairground booth or range where people fire at targets is a building given over to firing guns.

clue.text: Old village family created by Austen

definitions.meaning: an archaic word for a hamlet, surviving in English place names
John and Isabella and their kin in Northanger Abbey bear this surname

explanation.surface: A historic hamlet is home to a clan invented by Jane Austen.
explanation.definitionFit: The archaic word for a hamlet survives in place names, and it is the surname of Isabella and John in Northanger Abbey.

definitions.meaning: in cricket a captain asks a new bowler to bowl the next set of six balls
to come after someone in a role, replacing them

explanation.surface: A cricket captain asks the bowler to come on and win.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket an over is a set of six balls; the captain asks a bowler to bowl the next one.
explanation.definitionFit: Assuming control from a predecessor is succeeding them, and a captain asks a bowler to bowl the next six-ball spell.

parts.note: an artist who thinks of a work a second time paints it again, producing a duplicate

explanation.surface: A painter changes their mind and ends up with something new.
explanation.walkthrough: 'second thoughts' looks like a change of mind, but it means the artist doing the same picture a second time.
explanation.definitionFit: An exact copy of a painting made by the original artist is a duplicate, the work done again.

clue.text: In a crisis many involved with Greece avoid Athenian capital

indicators.note: involved means tangled up, so the letters are mixed together into a new order
avoid tells us to leave the named letter out of many
a capital is a head letter, here the first of Athenian

explanation.surface: Greece is in difficulty and many people steer clear of its capital, Athens.
explanation.walkthrough: 'avoid' takes the A ('Athenian capital') out of MANY, leaving MNY; 'involved with' mixes MNY with GREECE.
explanation.definitionFit: An emergency is a sudden dangerous situation needing urgent action, the same as a critical moment.

indicators.note: perhaps hints that the word reader could be rearranged into a different one

explanation.surface: A well-read, refined bookworm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cultivated' poses as refined, but it means raised, as crops or children.
explanation.definitionFit: Crops or livestock that have been grown or bred have been raised, brought up by a farmer.

clue.text: A day to remember — the tree fruited!

definitions.text: A day to remember — the tree fruited!

parts.words: A day to remember — the tree fruited!
parts.note: 29 May commemorates Charles II hiding in a tree, and the growth on that tree looks like a fruit

explanation.surface: A memorable day: the tree has finally borne fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: Oak Apple Day, 29 May, marks the restoration of Charles II, who hid in an oak; an oak apple is a round gall on an oak, not a real fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: The round gall caused by wasps on oak twigs looks like fruit, and gives its name to the 29 May Restoration holiday.

parts.note: vest is a waistcoat in American and older usage

indicators.note: say signals that a word is heard spoken, giving its sound

parts.note: meant means intended

explanation.surface: Was this waistcoat meant for Canon Chasuble of The Importance of Being Earnest?
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' makes MEANT sound like MENT. A chasuble is a priest's outer garment, and Canon Chasuble is the clergyman in Wilde's play, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: A chasuble is the sleeveless outer robe a priest wears at Mass, one example of ecclesiastical robes.

clue.text: Request for quiet on this trip would fail

definitions.text: Request for quiet on this trip would fail

parts.words: Request for quiet on this trip would fail
parts.note: the request for quiet is sh; placed on the word for this trip, it makes yelling, which defeats the request

explanation.surface: Asking for silence on this excursion would get nowhere.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is 'trip'; put SH in front and you get SHOUTING, which defeats any request for quiet.
explanation.definitionFit: A short pleasure trip or excursion, such as a day out to the seaside.

indicators.note: created means made anew, so the letters of the poet's name are formed into a new word

explanation.surface: A job specially made for the poet Keats.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Post' looks like a job, but it is a wooden stake.
explanation.definitionFit: A pointed wooden pole driven into the ground is a post.

clue.text: Evidence of ice on bonfire night

definitions.text: Evidence of ice on bonfire night

parts.words: Evidence of ice on bonfire night
parts.note: ice is slang for diamonds, which glitter, and hand-held fireworks are waved on 5 November

explanation.surface: Signs of frost on the night of the bonfire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ice' is slang for diamonds, which are also called sparklers; Bonfire Night (5 November, Guy Fawkes Night) is when British children wave hand-held fireworks.
explanation.definitionFit: Glittering diamonds are slangily called by this name, as are the spluttering hand-held fireworks waved on Guy Fawkes Night.

definitions.meaning: to amuse or please an audience
to consider an idea or suggestion

explanation.surface: Pleasure in pondering.
explanation.definitionFit: To amuse guests is to delight them, and to consider a proposal is to hold it in mind.

clue.text: Kindling as a sort of safeguard say

definitions.meaning: dry rotten wood used as tinder for lighting fires

definitions.text: as a sort of safeguard say
definitions.meaning: people say this phrase to ward off bad luck after boasting

explanation.surface: Gathering firewood as an insurance policy, so to speak.
explanation.walkthrough: As two words it is the superstitious saying used to avert bad luck.
explanation.definitionFit: Rotten dry wood serves as tinder for fires, and the two-word saying is uttered to ward off misfortune.

clue.text: Philosopher hard to please for the most part, but harmless

parts.note: Plato was the ancient Greek philosopher

indicators.note: most of the word is kept, its last letter dropped

parts.note: nice in its old sense means fastidious, fussy

explanation.surface: A thinker who is picky, mostly, but inoffensive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for the most part' drops the last letter of NICE, leaving NIC. 'nice' in its older sense means finicky.
explanation.definitionFit: A relationship that is affectionate but not sexual is innocent, without harm.

clue.text: Twelve houses are represented in this study

definitions.text: Twelve houses are represented in this study

parts.words: Twelve houses are represented in this study
parts.note: a horoscope divides the sky into twelve sectors called houses, used in reading the stars

explanation.surface: A survey of a street with twelve homes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'houses' suggests buildings, but in horoscopes the sky is divided into twelve houses.
explanation.definitionFit: Reading the stars divides the heavens into twelve houses, used to forecast human affairs.

clue.text: List is out but in the right order for Scotland

indicators.note: in tells us one piece goes inside the other
is out means the word list is put out of its proper order

explanation.surface: The list has gone astray, though it was in the correct sequence for the Scots.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is out' rearranges LIST to ISTL, which goes 'in' THE. The Order of the Thistle is Scotland's highest order of chivalry; 'right' is a fitting order.
explanation.definitionFit: The Most Ancient Order of the Thistle is Scotland's own order of knighthood, named after the national emblem.

definitions.meaning: a fruit cake is full of nuts, and a fruitcake is also a crazy person

explanation.surface: An underdone cake, like a fruit loaf.
explanation.definitionFit: A crazy person is slangily a fruitcake, and a fruit cake is full of kernels, so both senses mean crazy.

indicators.note: primarily means first of all, so the first letter of the is taken

parts.note: a reason is a motive

explanation.surface: Asks what mainly drove Guy Fawkes and his fellow plotters.
explanation.walkthrough: The Gunpowder Plot of 1605 was a plan to blow up Parliament and King James I, an act of treachery against the Crown.
explanation.definitionFit: Plotting to blow up king and Parliament was betrayal of the state, the crime against the Crown.

indicators.note: accepts means takes in, so one piece holds the other

parts.note: David Hume was the Scottish philosopher
BL is a Bachelor of Law

explanation.surface: An unassuming thinker takes a law qualification.
explanation.walkthrough: 'accepts' puts BL inside HUME.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone humble does not boast of their merits, which is what a modest person is.

definitions.meaning: a chess piece on the board
one of Chaucer's pilgrims telling a tale on the way to Canterbury

explanation.surface: A company director who tells stories in Canterbury.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Board member' suggests a director, but it is a chess piece. The Knight's Tale opens Chaucer's Canterbury Tales.
explanation.definitionFit: The horse-shaped chess piece moves on the board, and a chivalrous pilgrim tells the first of Chaucer's Canterbury Tales.

parts.note: the missing word completes a line from Hilaire Belloc's poem Dedicatory Ode

explanation.surface: A line of verse by Hilaire Belloc with a word missing.
explanation.walkthrough: Belloc's lines end 'There's nothing worth the wear of winning, / But laughter and the love of friends'; the blank is the missing word.
explanation.definitionFit: The fill-in-the-blank completes Belloc's line about mirth and friendship being the only things worth winning.

definitions.meaning: as a verb, to fill with delight or rapture

explanation.surface: A gate for vehicles.
explanation.walkthrough: Stressed on the second syllable it is a verb: to transport someone with delight.
explanation.definitionFit: A doorway is a way in, and to enchant someone carries them away with rapture.

parts.note: West, South and East are three of the four seats at a bridge table

explanation.surface: Provide a meal for a sibling and his card partners.
explanation.walkthrough: In bridge the players are named by compass points, so W, S and E are three of them.
explanation.definitionFit: Cattle that graze on leaves and shoots are eating, so to graze this way is to eat.

definitions.meaning: a fairground roller coaster ride is called this kind of railway

explanation.surface: A pretty branch line.
explanation.walkthrough: A scenic railway is an old British name for a roller coaster.
explanation.definitionFit: Countryside with fine views is pretty to look at, and an amusement-park roller coaster is a railway of that name.

definitions.meaning: producing a return, as an investment does

explanation.surface: Surrendering to the lure of money.
explanation.definitionFit: Submitting is surrendering, and an investment producing a return gives income.
